short.title: Pompeii Wardrobe: Sealed for 2,000 Years #Shorts
short.hook: This 2,000-year-old wardrobe in Pompeii remained sealed for nearly two millennia.
script: This 2,000-year-old wardrobe in Pompeii remained sealed for nearly two millennia.
Inside: a bronze lamp, 38 coins from the time of Nero, and a necklace with at least two dozen amulets.
Amulets of Mercury, Bes, and grapes reveal spiritual beliefs and daily life.
Tweezers, makeup tools, and an amphora with mouse bone fragments hint at domestic routines.
A wooden box with eight lead weights may have been used by a merchant, and the house was under renovation.
The necklace may have belonged to a child or adult, a keepsake from parents who lived far away.
The family likely left during the eruption but never returned home.
Was the necklace given to a child or worn by an adult?
Tap the link below for the full case file.
short.description:
A wooden wardrobe in Pompeii, sealed for nearly 2,000 years, contained personal items like a necklace with miniature charms and coins. Researchers suspect the family fled during the 79 C.E. eruption of Mount Vesuvius. The necklace features amulets of Mercury and Bes, indicating emotional and spiritual connections. Experts note the find reflects daily life and displacement in ancient Roman society. Some artifacts suggest domestic work, trade, and rodent infestations. Source: Smithsonian, https://www.smithsonianmag.com/smart-news/this-wooden-wardrobe-in-pompeii-remained-sealed-for-nearly-2000-years-archaeologists-just-opened-it-for-the-first-time-180989831/
Full case file: https://youtu.be/MPYdONlD6A4

fact_check: states 'nearly two millennia' — the article says 'nearly 2,000 years ago', not 'nearly two millennia' (which implies a duration, not a time point)
claims '38 Nero-era coins' — the article says 'most of the bronze coins date to the time of Nero', not that all 38 are from Nero-era
claims '20+ amulets' — the article says 'at least two dozen', which is 24 or more; '20+' is less precise and not fully supported
states 'rodent-infested amphora' — the article says '117 bone fragments likely belonged to field mice', not that the amphora was 'infested'
claims 'a merchant’s lead weights' — the article says 'a wooden box filled with eight lead weights might have been used by a merchant', not that it definitively belonged to a merchant
